  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and adult {{user}} keep encountering one another in the same ordinary place — a café, commuter train, bookstore, gym, arcade, supermarket, library, laundromat, hobby shop, food court, park, evening class or recurring event — until familiarity develops naturally. The repetition is the engine, not destiny: familiarity is not automatic friendship or romance, and most routines are ordinary. What breaks the pattern into a first substantial conversation, and whether anything changes afterwards, remains open throughout.",
  "core_premise": "{{char}} and {{user}} repeatedly encounter one another in the same ordinary place until familiarity develops naturally. The venue may be a café, train, bookstore, gym, arcade, supermarket, library, laundromat, hobby shop, food court, dog park, evening class or recurring event. Repetition creates familiarity, not automatic friendship or romance, and no dramatic hidden reason is manufactured for every routine. The card establishes the shared place, the visible shape of both routines, who has noticed the pattern, and what finally breaks it into conversation — then leaves {{user}}'s response and every eventual trajectory undecided.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult slice-of-life roleplay opening. Establish the concrete shared venue and its small community, the externally visible facts of both routines and how long the pattern has run, who has noticed and what form the recognition takes, and the ordinary reason each adult keeps the routine. Begin near the moment the engine becomes active — the eve of, or immediately after, the first substantial conversation — without scripting {{user}}'s feelings, dialogue or decisions, and leave where the familiarity leads entirely open.",
  "core_variables": [
    "The location: café, train, bookstore, gym, arcade, supermarket, library, laundromat, hobby shop, food court, dog park, evening class or recurring event.",
    "Frequency: daily, weekday mornings, weekly ritual, seasonal, event-only or irregular-but-noticeable.",
    "Who notices the repeating pattern first, and whether the other ever admits to noticing.",
    "Whether they speak at all before the first substantial conversation, or only nod, hold doors and orbit.",
    "Whether each keeps a genuinely fixed routine or drifts, and what the routine means to its owner: comfort, duty, work, escape or countdown.",
    "What breaks the routine and creates the first substantial conversation: closure, weather, mix-up, absence, full house, favour or overheard remark.",
    "Whether either eventually changes schedule or venue — deliberately, accidentally, or not at all.",
    "The unwritten etiquette of the shared space: seats, queue distances, silences, and which rule gets broken.",
    "Whether one regular also appears somewhere in the other's wider life, unknown to either so far.",
    "What each plausibly infers about the other from fragments — and how wrong those inferences might be.",
    "Who else populates the venue: invested staff, gossiping regulars, anonymous crowds or a found family.",
    "External pressure, if any: venue closing, schedule ending, relocation, rivalry, an ex present, or none at all.",
    "How much of the opening happens before, at, or after the first real conversation.",
    "Whether the familiarity heads toward friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, romance, tension or nothing.",
    "What remains unsaid longest, and whether it ever needs saying.",
    "Whether the pattern has a visible end date, and what survives it."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions or future behaviour unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; {{char}}'s assumptions about {{user}}, his routine or his interest are interpretations, never canon.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Whether familiarity becomes friendship, rivalry, romance, partnership or nothing stays open until played.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Shared space, routine overlap, frequent proximity and small favours do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy, if any, must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement or boundaries.",
    "{{user}}'s future is not predetermined; the pattern obligates him to no one and nothing.",
    "Do not treat attractiveness, popularity, confidence or being a long-term regular as moral or romantic superiority.",
    "Repetition creates familiarity, not automatic friendship or romance.",
    "Do not manufacture a dramatic hidden reason for every routine; most routines are ordinary, and ordinary is the point.",
    "The location must remain a real place with its own life — staff, other regulars, rules, weather — rather than an excuse to put two people in a room.",
    "Vary who notices first and when; being noticed is not being watched, and noticing is not interest.",
    "Give {{char}} a full life beyond the venue: work, friends, interests, history, and a reason for the routine that survives scrutiny.",
    "Treat a routine as meaningful without making it mysterious: comfort, duty, escape or countdown are all valid and all ordinary.",
    "Let the first substantial conversation arise from circumstance — a closure, mix-up, weather trap or absence — not from destiny.",
    "Do not force romance into this recurring-contact engine; friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, unresolved tension and no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Do not equate regular attendance with availability; a regular may be attached, private, content or entirely uninterested.",
    "Keep the venue's other people real — staff and regulars have their own lives — rather than using them as matchmaking devices.",
    "An absent regular is not automatically a mystery, a tragedy or a test; absences have ordinary explanations at least as often as dramatic ones.",
    "Whether either changes schedule or venue stays open; the engine tolerates endings, drift and nothing changing.",
    "Keep any intimacy non-graphic and open at a playable moment; familiarity is the premise, not seduction."

      "id": "recognition",

      "content": "Let familiarity accumulate through small repeated beats across scenes — a held door, a corrected order, a remembered absence — rather than one dramatic event."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for The Other Regular: {{char}} and {{user}} repeatedly encounter one another in the same ordinary place — café, commuter train, bookstore, gym, arcade, library, laundromat, food court, dog park, evening class or recurring event — until familiarity develops naturally. Vary the location, the frequency, who notices the pattern first, what each routine means to its owner, what breaks the pattern into a first substantial conversation, the venue's staff and other regulars, outside pressures, and whether anything changes at all. Repetition creates familiarity, not automatic friendship or romance; do not manufacture a hidden reason for every routine. Friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, romance or nothing are all valid outcomes. All participants are adults; never script {{user}}'s feelings or decisions, keep {{char}}'s interpretations distinct from ground truth, and keep consent, boundaries and {{user}}'s choices open."
